newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NGC sees higher profit, Aust expansion.
newsitem.headline: NGC sees higher profit, Aust expansion.

text.p: Natural Gas Corp chief executive Richard Bentley on Wednesday said the company's prediction of record gas sales in the 1996/97 year would lead to higher profits.
"You'd have to say yes," he told journalists at the conclusion of NGC's annual meeting, adding that it was not company policy to project future profit.
NGC posted an annual profit of NZ$28 million for the year to June, which was up from 22.2 million a year earlier.
Earlier, Bentley told shareholders that NGC gas sales could exceed 50 petajoules for the first time in the 1996/97 year.

The projection included an agreement, reached in the new competitive gas trading environment, for NGC to deliver five petajoules of gas to the Electricity Corporation of New Zealand (ECNZ) over the next 12 months for thermal power generation.
Bentley said the deal was a one-off transaction.
He said NGC would actively pursue offshore business opportunities and had targeted Australian pipelines in particular.
"We want to create shareholder wealth by expanding the business in areas in which we have true competency -- one of them is pipelines," he said.
"I think if you're a student of the Australian situation, there are a lot of pipelines up for sale of various kinds."
Asked how NGC would finance the expansion, Bentley said the company's balance sheet was strong.

"It's a strong balance sheet, infact the gearing of it is quite low after the debt we've repaid over the years, and if necessary we can always return to the shareholders if it's a good deal," he said.

NGC's current Maui gas supply arrangements end in 2009 and while Bentley agreed that future supply was an issue for the company, he was optimistic that new gas fields would be discovered, particularly in Taranaki.
"Taranaki is most under-explored by any normal standards. As the demand for gas starts to pick up, then they (explorers) will find gas because I believe they will be incentivised to do it," he said.
Bentley said the new wholesale electricity market launched on October 1 this year had opened up more opportunities in the cogeneration field.

"The wholesale electricity market provides a bit of a backstop now for cogeneration plants. They can sell electricity into the wholesale electricity market and it provides another step ahead, making it easier for cogeneration," he said.
He said NGC looked forward to new gas loads with the commencement of supply to the recently commissioned cogeneration plant at Bay Milks Edgecumbe factory.
NGC was also "working with a number of the possible developers" of the New Zealand Dairy Group's cogeneration plant at its Te Rapa site, but Bentley would not name them.
